title: What is AEO? Answer engine optimisation explained for Zimbabwean businesses
seo_title: What Is AEO? Answer Engine Optimisation in Zimbabwe
description: What AEO is, how ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, Perplexity and Google's AI choose their sources, and a practical checklist for Zimbabwean businesses.
intro: Ask an AI assistant to recommend a solar installer in Harare or a caterer in Bulawayo, and you get a short written answer instead of a page of links. A few businesses are named and the rest are left out. Answer engine optimisation (AEO) is the work of making sure AI tools can find your business, describe it accurately and have good reason to mention it. This guide explains how these tools choose their sources, what to fix first and how to measure the results.
body:
What AEO means

AEO stands for answer engine optimisation. It is also called GEO (generative engine optimisation) or AI search optimisation. All three describe the same job: helping AI assistants find your business, describe it correctly and send people your way.

Instead of scrolling through links, customers often get one written answer that names a few businesses. If you are not in it, they may never see you.

The AI tools that matter

  • ChatGPT search, which looks things up on the web and links to its sources.
  • Google AI Overviews and AI Mode, the AI answers inside Google Search.
  • Gemini, Google's assistant, which can draw on Google Search.
  • Microsoft Copilot, which draws on Bing.
  • Perplexity, an answer engine that links to the websites it uses.
  • Meta AI, Meta's assistant, which can cite and link to web pages in its answers.
  • Claude, Anthropic's assistant, which can also search the web.

How AI tools find and choose sources

  1. Search indexes. Google says AI Overviews and AI Mode pull pages from its Search index and may run several related searches at once ("query fan-out"). OpenAI, Perplexity, Anthropic and Meta run their own search crawlers too.
  2. Live browsing. An assistant may open a page there and then to answer a question.
  3. Training data. Models learn from text gathered before a cut-off date, which is why an old phone number can linger long after you change it.

Each route rewards the same thing: clear, consistent, well-supported information. When your website, Google Business Profile, social pages and directories agree on your name, location, services and contact details, AI tools have less room to get you wrong.

AEO builds on SEO and local SEO

AEO does not replace SEO. Google's own guide says optimising for its generative AI features is still SEO, and tells site owners to put effective SEO ahead of "AEO/GEO hacks". It says there is no need to chop content into tiny chunks, and that chasing inauthentic mentions is not as helpful as it might seem. Google also says a page must be indexed and eligible for a snippet to appear as a supporting link in its AI answers.

So the foundations come first: a sound, well-optimised website (see our SEO service) and a strong presence on Google Maps and local listings (see our local SEO service). AEO work then checks how AI tools describe you and closes the gaps.

A practical checklist for Zimbabwean businesses

1. Make your business facts identical everywhere

List your official name, phone and WhatsApp numbers, email, address or service area, hours and main services. Check them on your website, Google Business Profile, Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp Business and directories. Fix old numbers, closed branches and discontinued services.

2. Keep your Google Business Profile complete

Google's advice for its AI features includes keeping your Business Profile information up to date. Choose accurate categories, add services, hours and photos, and reply to reviews.

3. Earn reviews and mentions on trusted local sites

Ask real customers for Google reviews, for example by WhatsApp after each job. Never buy, fake or reward reviews: Google's policies prohibit it. Then look for genuine mentions on Zimbabwean news sites, industry association and chamber of commerce pages, and partner websites. Independent sources that agree with your site back it up.

4. Answer real customer questions on your website

List the questions people ask in WhatsApp chats and calls before they buy, such as "Do you deliver to Gweru?" or "Which payment methods do you accept?" Answer each one plainly, in text. Add what only you can say: your prices, process and local experience. Google's guide favours original, first-hand content over generic material anyone could write.

5. Add structured data, with honest expectations

Structured data (schema markup) labels the facts on a page for machines. Use Organization or LocalBusiness markup for your name, logo, address, phone and hours, and FAQPage markup only for questions and answers visible on the page. Google says structured data is not required for its AI features and there is no special markup to add. It is still sound SEO practice, provided every detail matches what visitors see.

6. Let the right AI crawlers in

Your robots.txt file tells crawlers what they may visit, and most AI companies use separate crawlers for search and for training.

NameCompanyWhat it controls
GooglebotGoogleGoogle Search, including AI Overviews and AI Mode. Never block it.
Google-ExtendedGoogleA robots.txt token, not a crawler. Covers Gemini model training and grounding in Gemini apps. No effect on Google Search.
BingbotMicrosoftBing search, which Copilot draws on.
OAI-SearchBotOpenAIAppearing in ChatGPT search answers.
GPTBotOpenAIUse of your content to train OpenAI's models.
PerplexityBotPerplexityBeing shown and linked in Perplexity's answers.
Claude-SearchBotAnthropicIndexing for Claude's search results.
ClaudeBotAnthropicUse of your content to train Anthropic's models.
Meta-WebIndexerMetaBeing cited and linked in Meta AI's answers.

User-triggered fetchers such as ChatGPT-User, Claude-User and Perplexity-User visit a page on someone's behalf, when their question needs a live look at it. OpenAI and Perplexity say robots.txt may not apply to theirs, because a person made the request.

Allow the search crawlers if you want to be recommended. Blocking GPTBot or ClaudeBot is a separate choice about training; Google-Extended needs more thought, as it also covers Gemini grounding. Google also advises checking that your CDN and hosting set-up allow crawling.

7. Treat llms.txt as optional

llms.txt is a plain-text summary of your site for AI tools, proposed in 2024. Google says Google Search does not use it, though having one is fine. The crawler guidance from OpenAI, Anthropic and Perplexity centres on robots.txt instead. We add one in our AEO work because it is quick and harmless, but it will not fix unclear content or inconsistent details.

8. Keep pages fast and accessible

Many customers browse on phones over mobile data, so keep pages light. Google recommends making important content available as text: put key details in real text on your pages, not only in image flyers or scanned PDFs. Use clear headings, alt text and labelled buttons: OpenAI says its ChatGPT Atlas browser uses ARIA tags to understand pages, so accessible markup helps people and AI agents alike.

How to measure AI referrals in GA4

Google Analytics 4 now has an AI Assistant channel in its default channel group, covering visits from sources such as ChatGPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, Copilot and Grok. In the Traffic acquisition report, find the AI Assistant row and add Session source as a secondary dimension to see which assistants sent visitors (for example chatgpt.com, gemini.google.com or copilot.microsoft.com). OpenAI says ChatGPT automatically adds utm_source=chatgpt.com to referral links, which helps you spot those visits.

  • Google's AI features are separate. The channel excludes AI Overviews and AI Mode, whose clicks count as Organic Search. For those, use Search Console's Generative AI performance report, which may not appear until your site has enough AI impressions.
  • Check other assistants. If perplexity.ai or claude.ai visits sit under Referral, add them to your AI total. For Copilot citations, see the AI Performance report in Bing Webmaster Tools.
  • Expect gaps. Some AI visits arrive with no source, for example when someone copies your link into a browser, and GA4 counts them as Direct.

Track form submissions, WhatsApp clicks and clicks on your phone number as key events to see whether AI visitors get in touch; our GA4 checklist covers the set-up. Then test by hand: put the same buyer questions to each tool monthly and note who gets named.

Finally, ask people. Add "AI assistant (ChatGPT, Gemini and so on)" to your "How did you hear about us?" options, and ask on calls and WhatsApp too, because some people read an AI answer and then message you directly.

What not to expect

  • No guarantees. No one can promise that an AI assistant will recommend your business. Answers vary with the question's wording, the person asking, their location and the day. Google says no third-party tool has access to its internal ranking or AI systems.
  • No overnight fixes. Search-based answers can reflect changes once pages are recrawled, but what a model learned in training changes only when it is retrained.
  • No shortcuts. Avoid anyone selling guaranteed spots in AI answers, bulk mentions or reviews. They put your reputation at risk. Paid ads inside AI assistants, such as ChatGPT ads, are a separate channel.

To see how AI tools describe your business today, explore our AEO service or get in touch.
faqs: Will blocking GPTBot keep my business out of ChatGPT?

Not by itself. GPTBot is OpenAI's training crawler, so blocking it tells OpenAI not to use your content to train its models. Appearing in ChatGPT search answers is managed separately, through OAI-SearchBot. You can block GPTBot and still allow OAI-SearchBot.
Do I need an llms.txt file for AEO?

It's optional. Google says Google Search doesn't use llms.txt files, though having one is fine, and the crawler guidance from OpenAI, Anthropic and Perplexity is built around robots.txt. The file is quick to add, so we include one, but consistent business facts, clear answers and the right robots.txt settings matter far more.
How can I tell if AI assistants are sending me customers?

Use three sources together: the AI Assistant channel in Google Analytics 4, the Generative AI performance report in Google Search Console for Google's own AI features, and a simple question to every new customer about how they found you. No single number tells the whole story, because some people read an AI answer and then contact you directly.

title: ChatGPT ads explained: what Zimbabwean businesses need to know
seo_title: ChatGPT Ads Explained for Zimbabwean Businesses
description: What ChatGPT ads are, who can buy them as of November 2026, where Zimbabwe stands, and how to get ready with tracking, landing pages and AEO.
intro: ChatGPT now shows ads in some countries, and Zimbabwean business owners are asking whether they should be there. As of November 2026, the short answer is not yet, if your business is registered only in Zimbabwe. This guide explains what ChatGPT ads are, where they appear, who can buy them, how they differ from AEO and Google Ads, and what you can do now so you're ready if things change.
body:
What ChatGPT ads are

ChatGPT ads are paid placements inside ChatGPT, OpenAI's AI assistant. OpenAI began testing them in the US in February 2026 and has since added more countries in stages.

An ad appears below ChatGPT's answer, in its own card labelled "Sponsored". It is matched to what the conversation is about, so someone asking for help choosing a laptop might see an electronics retailer's ad under the answer. OpenAI says ads do not change ChatGPT's answers. Advertisers see only overall figures, such as views and clicks, and never anyone's chats.

Who sees them

Not everyone who uses ChatGPT. As of November 2026:

  • Ads are shown only to adults on ChatGPT's Free and Go plans, in the countries where OpenAI runs ads.
  • People on the Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise and Education plans don't see ads.
  • No ads go to users who say they are under 18, or whom OpenAI predicts are under 18.
  • Ads are kept away from sensitive conversations, such as those about health, mental health and politics.

Who can buy them, as of November 2026

OpenAI sells ChatGPT ads country by country, from a list it updates often. As of November 2026 it covers the US and countries across the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia-Pacific, including the UK and Australia, where many Zimbabweans live. OpenAI has also announced South Africa as a market, but we confirm it on OpenAI's current list before planning any campaign there.

Zimbabwe is not on the list. In practice, that means:

  • A business registered only in Zimbabwe can't buy ChatGPT ads yet. The business that advertises, and pays, has to be based in an eligible country.
  • Ads can't be aimed at people in Zimbabwe either.
  • Diaspora campaigns are possible through an eligible business. If your group already has a company that is genuinely registered and trading in the UK or Australia, for example, that company may be able to open its own account. A new account may only be able to advertise in its own country at first.

Two cautions. Don't register a company abroad just to get access, and be wary of anyone who offers to arrange it. And ChatGPT ads can't single out "Zimbabweans" as a group: targeting works by location, the topic of the conversation and, in some cases, your own customer lists.

Where ads are available, businesses buy them through OpenAI's self-serve Ads Manager or its technology partners. If we manage the campaigns, the ad spend is still paid directly to OpenAI from the advertising company's own account.

How ChatGPT ads compare with AEO and Google Ads

ChatGPT adsOrganic AI answers (AEO)Google Ads
Available to a business registered only in ZimbabweNoYesYes
Reaches people in ZimbabweNoYesYes
Reaches South Africa, the UK, the US and AustraliaYes, in the UK, the US and Australia, through a business registered thereYesYes
Where you appearA "Sponsored" card below the answerNamed or linked inside the answerGoogle Search, YouTube, partner websites and apps, and Shopping
What you payAd spend, paid directly to OpenAINo ad spend; you invest in your website, content and reputationAd spend, paid directly to Google

Ads versus organic answers

A ChatGPT ad sits under the answer. It never puts your business inside the answer. Being named in the answer itself has to be earned, and answer engine optimisation (AEO) is that work: making your business easy for AI tools to find, understand and trust. Our guide, What is AEO?, explains how it works.

The two also reach different people. Organic answers reach every ChatGPT user, including people in Zimbabwe and people on paid plans who never see ads. Ads stop when your budget stops. Organic visibility builds over time, though nobody can guarantee it. For a Zimbabwean business, AEO is the part of ChatGPT you can work on today.

ChatGPT ads versus Google Ads

Google Ads is open to Zimbabwean businesses now. You can run Search, Display, YouTube, Shopping, Performance Max, Demand Gen and App campaigns aimed at Zimbabwe and at diaspora markets. Google search ads are triggered by what people type, while ChatGPT ads are matched to a whole conversation in which people often describe exactly what they need.

Google's and Microsoft's AI features can carry ads too. Eligible Google Ads campaigns can show in Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode, and eligible Microsoft Advertising campaigns can show in Copilot, in the countries where those placements are offered. Nobody can buy a guaranteed spot inside an AI answer. See our Google Ads and Microsoft Ads services for what's possible today.

How to get ready now

1. Get your tracking right

Whatever platform comes next, you'll need to know which clicks became customers. Set up Google Analytics 4 with key events for WhatsApp clicks, calls, enquiry forms and sales, and tag every ad link with UTM parameters. GA4 also groups visits from ChatGPT and other assistants into an AI Assistant channel. Our GA4 checklist covers the set-up.

2. Build landing pages that carry on the conversation

People who click from ChatGPT have often asked detailed questions first. Your page should answer the next ones: the price or price range, what's included, delivery areas and times, how buyers abroad can pay, and proof such as photos and genuine reviews. Make one page per offer and per country, keep it fast on mobile, and add a WhatsApp button with your full international number.

3. Sharpen your offers

An ad under a detailed answer has to add something the answer didn't. "Quality service at affordable prices" won't. Specific, checkable offers will: a fixed delivery fee to Bulawayo, an itemised quote on WhatsApp within the hour, or a video call to view a stand before paying. Write a few short headlines and descriptions for each.

4. Work on organic AEO

Make your business details identical everywhere, answer real customer questions on your website, earn genuine reviews, and let OpenAI's search crawler, OAI-SearchBot, into your site.

5. Check your industry's rules

OpenAI's ad policies keep some industries out and add extra checks for others. If you work in a regulated field such as health, finance, alcohol or gambling, read the current policy before planning anything.

What to watch for

  • OpenAI's country list. It changes often, so we check it before planning any campaign.
  • New formats. OpenAI has been testing new ad formats in the US. Don't assume they will reach other countries soon.
  • Promises that don't add up. Be wary of anyone selling "ChatGPT ads in Zimbabwe" today, or a guaranteed place inside ChatGPT's answers.
  • Other AI assistants. Perplexity phased out its ads in February 2026, and as of November 2026 there is no ad placement to buy inside the Gemini app, Meta AI or Claude.

Want to be ready if OpenAI opens ChatGPT ads to more countries? We can prepare your ad creative and landing pages now. See our ChatGPT ads service or talk to us.
faqs: Can a business in Zimbabwe advertise on ChatGPT?

Not as of November 2026. OpenAI sells ChatGPT ads only to businesses based in the countries on its list, and Zimbabwe isn't one of them. Ads can't be aimed at people in Zimbabwe yet either. A related company that is genuinely registered and trading in an eligible country, such as the UK or Australia, may be able to advertise there through its own account.
Will paying for ChatGPT ads make ChatGPT recommend my business?

No. OpenAI says ads don't change ChatGPT's answers. Ads appear separately, below the answer, labelled "Sponsored". Being named in the answer itself depends on how well AI tools can find, understand and trust your business, which is the job of answer engine optimisation (AEO).
Do all ChatGPT users see ads?

No. As of November 2026, ads are shown only to adults on the Free and Go plans, in the countries where OpenAI runs ads. People on the Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise and Education plans don't see them, and OpenAI keeps ads away from sensitive conversations such as health, mental health and politics.

title: GA4 setup checklist for Zimbabwean business websites
seo_title: GA4 Setup Checklist for Zimbabwean Websites
description: A practical GA4 setup checklist for Zimbabwean businesses: currency, key events, WhatsApp and call tracking, consent, AI referrals and monthly reviews.
intro: Google Analytics 4 (GA4) is free, but a quick install mostly tells you how many people visited and which pages they viewed. It won't show how many people tapped your WhatsApp or call buttons, sent an enquiry or bought something unless you set it up to. This checklist takes Zimbabwean business owners and marketing managers through a proper setup, from creating the property to a monthly review. Use it on a new website or to audit the property you already have.
body:
1. Create the property and web data stream

  • Create it under a Google account your business owns, then add your agency or developer as users.
  • In Admin, click Create, then Property. Pick your industry, business size and objectives, which decide the reports you see first.
  • Under Data collection and modification, open Data streams, click Add stream, choose Web and enter your domain.
  • Copy the Measurement ID (it starts with G-) for your tag.

2. Set the time zone and currency

Time zone: choose Zimbabwe, so report days match your working day. Changing it later affects only new data.

Currency: choose USD. GA4 converts only the currencies on its supported list, and when we checked in November 2026, ZWG (Zimbabwe Gold) wasn't on it. If you sell in ZWG, convert to USD in your website code before the value reaches GA4. If you send prices in rand, pounds or another supported currency, GA4 converts them to USD at the previous day's exchange rate.

3. Turn on enhanced measurement, and know its limits

In your web stream's settings, make sure Enhanced measurement is on. With no extra code it records page views, scrolls (only when a visitor reaches 90 per cent of the way down a page), outbound clicks, site searches, embedded YouTube plays (if the player's JavaScript API is on), file downloads such as PDF price lists, and form starts and submissions.

It won't give WhatsApp, call or email clicks their own named events, confirm a submitted form actually reached you, or record sales.

4. Install the tag once

  • Google tag: paste the snippet into the head of every page, or use your platform's built-in Google integration.
  • Google Tag Manager: add a tag for your G- ID that fires on every page. We prefer Tag Manager: the click tracking below is easier to build there.

Use one method, not both, or you risk counting visits twice. Check it with Tag Assistant and the Realtime report, allowing up to 30 minutes for new data.

5. Track WhatsApp, calls, emails and forms

In Tag Manager, give each enquiry action its own event:

  • WhatsApp: a Just Links click trigger where Click URL contains wa.me (add api.whatsapp.com if your buttons use it), firing a GA4 event named whatsapp_click.
  • Calls: Click URL starts with tel:, event phone_click.
  • Email: Click URL starts with mailto:, event email_click.
  • Forms: generate_lead, Google's recommended event for leads, sent only on a confirmed submission, such as the thank-you page loading.

No Tag Manager? GA4's Create event option can build whatsapp_click from outbound clicks whose link_url contains wa.me. Never send names, phone numbers or email addresses to GA4: Google requires you to keep personally identifiable information out.

6. Mark key events

GA4 calls your important actions key events. Google Ads calls them conversions. Mark an action as a key event in GA4, then, once Google Ads is linked, create a conversion from it so campaigns can optimise towards it.

  • When your events appear, open Admin, then Events under Data display, and click the star beside each one. Free properties allow up to 30 key events.
  • Mark business actions only: whatsapp_click, phone_click, email_click, generate_lead and, for shops, purchase.
  • Consider "once per session" counting for leads, so someone tapping WhatsApp three times counts once.
  • Key events count from when you mark them, not before.

7. Filter out your team and developers

  • In the web stream's tag settings, define internal traffic using your office's fixed IP address, then test and activate the Internal traffic filter under Data filters.
  • Create and activate a Developer traffic filter too, so test visits sent in debug mode stay out.
  • IP rules mainly catch staff on fixed office lines, because mobile data addresses change often.
  • Active filters are permanent: GA4 doesn't keep the data they exclude.

8. Extend data retention

In Admin, open Data retention. If event data retention says 2 months, change it to 14 months, the longest a free property allows. The setting affects explorations and funnel reports, not standard reports. Do it on day one: data that has already expired can't be brought back.

9. Cross-domain measurement and unwanted referrals

If visitors move between your own domains, such as your main site and a separate shop, add them all under Configure your domains in the tag settings, so GA4 sees one journey. If customers pay on a payment gateway's own domain and return to your thank-you page, add that domain under List unwanted referrals, so the gateway doesn't take credit for sales.

10. Link Google Ads and Search Console

  • Google Ads: in Admin, under Product links, link your Ads account, keep auto-tagging on, and create conversions from your key events. Our Google Ads management includes this as standard.
  • Search Console: link your verified site to see Google search queries and landing pages in GA4, then publish the Search Console reports from the Library.

11. Add e-commerce events for online stores

Send the standard events, including view_item, add_to_cart, begin_checkout and purchase. Each purchase needs a unique transaction_id, the value, the currency and the items. Shop plugins can send these, but place a real test order and check it arrives once, in USD, with the right amount. If many orders close on WhatsApp, track WhatsApp clicks from product pages too, so you can at least see which products start those conversations.

12. Consent and Consent Mode for UK and EU visitors

This matters whenever your site gets visitors from the UK or Europe, and especially if you advertise to Zimbabweans living there. Google's EU user consent policy covers visitors in the European Economic Area (EEA), the UK and Switzerland. You need their consent for personalised ads, and for measurement where the law requires it.

  • Consent Mode passes each visitor's choice to Google's tags. Version 2 added ad_user_data and ad_personalization alongside the original ad_storage and analytics_storage.
  • For EEA visitors, Google requires these signals, via Consent Mode or the IAB's consent framework (TCF), to keep its measurement, remarketing and personalised ads features working. It says it doesn't expect a verified signal for UK or Swiss traffic, but UK privacy law still applies.
  • Consent Mode isn't a banner. Pair it with a consent management platform that supports Consent Mode.
  • Basic mode keeps Google's tags off until the visitor agrees, and sends nothing if they decline. Advanced mode sends cookieless pings while consent is denied, so Google can model some of the gaps.
  • Since 15 June 2026, Consent Mode settings in Google Ads, not GA4's Google signals setting, control whether Google Ads cookies and IDs are collected through your GA4 tag.

13. See visits from AI assistants

GA4's default channel group now includes an AI Assistant channel for visits from tools such as ChatGPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, Copilot and Grok. Find it in the Traffic acquisition report under Reports. It excludes Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode, which GA4 counts as Organic Search.

If an assistant your buyers use, such as Perplexity or Claude, still lands in Referral, create a custom channel group under Admin, Data display, Channel groups: copy the default group, add a channel where Source matches the regex .*(perplexity|claude)\.ai.*, and place it above Referral so it matches first. Treat totals as a minimum: some visits arrive with no source. Getting named in those answers is the job of AEO.

14. Build a Data Studio dashboard

Data Studio (formerly Looker Studio) is Google's free dashboard tool, and it connects directly to GA4. Build one page your team will read: key events by channel and by type, top landing pages, AI Assistant visits and Search Console queries.

15. Monthly review routine

  1. On mobile data rather than office Wi-Fi, tap your own WhatsApp button and phone link, and check both appear in Realtime. Your internal traffic filter hides visits from the office.
  2. Compare key events by channel with last month and the same month last year.
  3. Find landing pages with plenty of visits but few key events, and fix those first. That is where conversion rate optimisation pays off.
  4. Review AI Assistant visits and Search Console queries.
  5. Compare GA4 key events with Google Ads conversions and look into big gaps.
  6. Annotate site changes, price changes and campaign launches.

Common mistakes

  • Sending ZWG prices labelled as USD, which inflates revenue.
  • Leaving data retention at 2 months.
  • Treating enhanced measurement's form_submit as confirmed leads.
  • Marking page views or scrolls as key events.
  • Letting an agency or freelancer own the account.
  • Remarketing to UK and EU visitors with no consent setup.

Our Google Analytics and tracking service can audit your property against this list.
faqs: Should my GA4 property use USD or ZWG?

Use USD. GA4 only converts currencies on its supported list, and when we checked in November 2026, ZWG was not on it. If you sell in ZWG, convert prices to USD in your website code before they are sent to GA4, so your revenue figures stay accurate.
What is the difference between a key event and a conversion?

A key event is an action you mark as important in GA4, such as a WhatsApp click or a completed enquiry form. A conversion is what Google Ads uses to measure and optimise your campaigns. Once GA4 and Google Ads are linked, you can create Google Ads conversions from your key events.
Can GA4 show visits from ChatGPT and other AI assistants?

Yes. GA4's default channel group now includes an AI Assistant channel for visits from tools such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Copilot. It doesn't cover Google's AI Overviews or AI Mode, and some visits arrive without a source, so treat the figure as a minimum.

title: Click-to-WhatsApp ads: a practical guide for Zimbabwean businesses
seo_title: How to Run Click-to-WhatsApp Ads in Zimbabwe
description: How to run Click-to-WhatsApp ads in Zimbabwe: app or Platform, linking accounts, objectives, pre-filled messages, fast replies, tracking and costs.
intro: For many Zimbabwean customers, WhatsApp is where buying decisions happen. A Click-to-WhatsApp ad on Facebook or Instagram opens a chat with your business in one tap, so people can ask a question, get a price and order without visiting a website. This guide covers the set-up choices, the ad itself, your first replies, the handover to sales and how to measure what your money brings back.
body:
What a Click-to-WhatsApp ad is

A Click-to-WhatsApp ad is a Facebook or Instagram ad with a button that opens a WhatsApp chat with your business. It can run in feeds, Stories and Marketplace. Instead of landing on a website, the customer lands in a chat with a message ready to send.

Businesses based in Zimbabwe can run these ads and aim them at people in Zimbabwe or in diaspora markets such as South Africa, the UK, the US and Australia. You pay your ad spend directly to Meta, which charges as the ad is shown, not per chat, so an ad few people act on costs more per conversation.

Ads in WhatsApp Status can open a chat too, but they're bought alongside Instagram Stories and aren't offered everywhere (not in the UK or the EU, for example), so check Ads Manager first.

Step 1: Choose the WhatsApp Business app or the Platform

Both work with Click-to-WhatsApp ads. The difference is how you handle the chats.

WhatsApp Business appWhatsApp Business Platform
SuitsSmall businesses with one number and a small teamLarger teams, several branches or high chat volumes
Set-upA free app on your phoneThrough a provider, or a direct connection built by developers
CostFree to useMeta charges per message, and providers may add their own fees
ToolsBusiness profile, greeting and away messages, quick replies, labels, catalogue, broadcastsMessage templates, list and reply buttons, automated flows with handover to staff, CRM connections

On the Platform, these pricing rules apply as of November 2026:

  • Template messages, such as offers and order updates, are charged even inside the customer service window: the 24 hours after the customer's last message. The exception is the free window described below.
  • Since 1 October 2026, Meta also charges for service messages (your ordinary replies). Rates vary by country code, with Zimbabwe's +263 numbers in Meta's "Rest of Africa" group. Check the current rate card, and any free allowance, before you budget.
  • When someone messages you from a Click-to-WhatsApp ad using WhatsApp on their phone, and you reply within 24 hours, a free entry point window opens and can stay open for up to seven days. Meta doesn't charge for your replies or templates in it.

Start with the app while you test. Move to the Platform when a busy team must share one number or you want automation and a CRM link, and plan the move with your provider. Our email and WhatsApp marketing team sets up both.

Step 2: Connect WhatsApp to your Facebook Page and Instagram

  • Choose one business number that is always answered, and use it everywhere: ads, website, Google profile and receipts.
  • Connect it to the Facebook Page that will run your ads, in the Page's settings, and confirm that you control the number. If the menus have moved, Meta's Help Centre has the current steps.
  • Connect your Instagram professional account to the same Page or business portfolio, so the ads can also run on Instagram under your Instagram name.
  • Make sure the business owns the Page, ad account and number, and add staff as people and your agency as a partner in your business portfolio.

Step 3: Choose the right campaign objective

In Ads Manager, Click-to-WhatsApp ads can run under the Engagement, Leads, Sales or Traffic objective. Set the conversion location to messaging apps, choose WhatsApp, and match the objective to your goal:

Your goalObjectiveOptimise for
Enquiries, quotes and bookingsEngagement or LeadsConversations
Product ordersSalesConversations at first, then purchases once you report sales back to Meta

Don't optimise for link clicks, reach or impressions: Meta will then look for people likely to tap or see the ad, not start a chat. Meta advises running an ad for at least seven days, so don't change it daily. Target only the towns you serve, and give each diaspora country its own campaign.

Step 4: Write the ad and the pre-filled message

A good ad tells people what you sell, roughly what it costs, which areas you serve and what happens when they tap, for example: "Tap for a quote on WhatsApp. We reply within 15 minutes, 7am to 9pm." Only promise what your team can keep, and use real photos or short videos.

The pre-filled message is the text waiting in the chat box, which the customer can edit before sending. Meta's default, "Hello! Can I get more info on this?", tells you nothing. Write your own, with a short reference for each ad so your team knows which one brought the chat:

  • "Hi, I'd like a quote for a home solar system in Harare. (Ref: SOLAR-HRE)"
  • "Hi, please send this week's hamper list for delivery to Bulawayo. (Ref: HAMPER-UK)"

Step 5: Set up your greeting and quick replies

In the WhatsApp Business app, set up:

  • A greeting message, sent automatically when a new customer messages you. Thank them, say when a person will reply, and ask the one question that helps most, such as their area.
  • An away message for outside your hours, with an honest reply time.
  • Quick replies for prices, delivery areas and fees, payment methods (including for buyers abroad), your location and hours, and how to order.
  • A catalogue with photos and prices, so people can browse while they wait.

On the Platform, your provider can add list and reply buttons and simple automated flows. Always offer a quick way to reach a person.

Step 6: Answer fast

Someone who has just tapped your ad is at their most interested. Keep them waiting and they may message a competitor instead.

  • Put someone in charge of the chats whenever ads are running, with a rota for evenings and weekends.
  • Diaspora buyers message in their own time: a buyer in the US may write while you're asleep, and evenings in Australia fall in your late morning or early afternoon.
  • On the Platform, reply within 24 hours to open the free entry point window. Once 24 hours pass after the customer's last message, you can only send approved templates.

Step 7: Hand over to sales

  • Agree who owns each chat and when it passes to a salesperson.
  • Collect the same details every time: name, area, what they need, budget, timing and how they will pay.
  • Label every chat, for example new lead, quote sent, paid and delivered.
  • Put quotes and invoices in writing.
  • Log each lead and its ad reference in one place: a CRM or, to start with, a simple spreadsheet.

Step 8: Measure conversations and sales

Ads Manager shows how many conversations your ads started and what each cost. Your own records show how many became sales. Each week, for each ad reference:

  1. Count the chats, quotes and sales.
  2. Divide ad spend by sales to get your cost per sale.
  3. Compare it with your profit per sale.
  4. Move budget to the ads with the lowest cost per sale, not the cheapest chats.

On the Platform, ask your provider whether it can send confirmed sales back to Meta through the Conversions API, so Ads Manager can report, and optimise for, purchases rather than just chats. For ads that go to your website first, track WhatsApp clicks as key events in Google Analytics 4 (see our GA4 checklist).

Common mistakes

  • Leaving Meta's default pre-filled message, so you can't tell your ads apart.
  • Judging success by cost per chat instead of cost per sale.
  • Vague ads with no price, area or offer, which bring chats from people you can't serve.
  • Using a staff member's personal number instead of one the business controls.
  • Adding everyone who messages to broadcasts without asking first.

Want help setting up or running your campaigns? See our WhatsApp ads service or get in touch.
faqs: Do I need the WhatsApp Business Platform to run Click-to-WhatsApp ads?

No. Click-to-WhatsApp ads work with the free WhatsApp Business app, which suits most small businesses starting out. The Platform makes sense when a busy team needs to share the same number, or when you want automation and a CRM connection. Meta charges per message on the Platform, but messages are free during the window of up to seven days that opens when you reply to an ad chat within 24 hours.
How much do Click-to-WhatsApp ads cost?

You choose the budget in Meta Ads Manager and pay your ad spend directly to Meta. Meta charges as your ad is shown, so your cost per chat depends on your targeting, your offer and how many people go on to message you. The WhatsApp Business app itself is free to use. On the Platform, Meta charges per message, by message type and by the country of the number you message, apart from free messages, such as those sent in the window of up to seven days that opens when you reply to an ad chat within 24 hours.
Can Click-to-WhatsApp ads reach Zimbabweans living abroad?

Yes. Target the countries or cities where your buyers live, such as Johannesburg, London or Sydney, and make the ad clearly about Zimbabwe, for example groceries delivered to Harare. We don't target people by nationality. We use location, your own customer lists and ads that clearly speak to people buying for family at home. Run a separate campaign for each country, and reply during the buyer's waking hours.

title: How to get your Zimbabwean business on Google Maps and rank locally
seo_title: Local SEO Zimbabwe: How to Get on Google Maps and Rank
description: A step-by-step guide to getting your Zimbabwean business onto Google Maps: profile setup, verification, categories, reviews, listings and tracking.
intro: When someone in Harare searches for a plumber, a pharmacy or a hardware store, Google often shows a map and a short list of nearby businesses before any ordinary website. Getting onto that map is free. Showing up well on it takes care and steady work. This guide covers each step in the order we'd tackle it, from setting up your Google Business Profile to tracking the calls it brings in.
body:
How Google decides which businesses to show

Google says local results depend on three things: relevance (how well your profile matches the search), distance (how far you are from the searcher, or from the place they named) and prominence (how well known and well reviewed you are, online and off). You can't change your distance from every customer, but most of the steps below improve relevance, prominence or both.

Step 1: Claim or create your Google Business Profile

First, search for your business on Google Maps. If a listing already exists, claim it rather than creating a duplicate, which would split your reviews and confuse customers.

  • Use a Google account owned by the business, not by a member of staff, and add a second owner or manager so you're never locked out.
  • Use your real business name, exactly as it appears on your signboard and invoices. Adding extra words, such as "Cheap Plumber Harare 24hrs", breaks Google's guidelines and can get a profile suspended.

Getting verified

Google decides which verification methods you're offered, and for many businesses it's now a short phone video. Film one continuous clip, with no editing, showing:

  • the street outside, nearby landmarks and your signage
  • the business at work: equipment, stock, branded vehicles or uniforms
  • proof that you run it, such as unlocking the door, opening the till or showing business documents

If it fails, follow Google's instructions, fix what was missing and try again, rather than opening a new profile.

Step 2: Choose your categories carefully

Your primary category is one of the most important choices you'll make. Pick the most specific option for your main business: "Hardware store" tells Google far more than "Store". Add secondary categories only for other things you genuinely do. The categories shown under competitors on the map are a useful guide. Then fill in the Services section, with a short description of each service and, where you can, a starting price.

Step 3: Shopfront or service area?

If customers come to you, show your address and check the map pin. Where street numbers are missing or unclear, drag the pin to your exact gate and put clear directions on your website's contact page.

If you travel to customers and don't serve them at your premises, as many plumbers, solar installers and home-based businesses do, hide your address and set a service area. List the towns or suburbs you really cover, for example Harare, Chitungwiza and Ruwa. Google's guidelines ask you to stay within about two hours' drive of your base, and profiles tend to show most strongly near their base. Only open a second profile where you have real, staffed premises. Reach other towns through location pages instead (see Step 8).

Step 4: Complete every section and add real photos

  • Phone: a number that's always answered. If it's on WhatsApp too, say so on your website.
  • Hours: your normal hours, plus special hours for public holidays such as Independence Day and Christmas.
  • Website: your homepage or, for a branch, that branch's own page.
  • Description: up to 750 characters on what you do, where and for whom, in plain language.
  • Photos: your logo, a cover photo, your premises from the street, the inside, your team, products and finished jobs. Use real photos, not stock images, and add new ones monthly.

Step 5: Post updates regularly

Google lets you publish short posts on your profile, such as updates, offers and events. A post every week or two, with a photo you took, shows people you're open and active. Ideas include new stock, a finished installation in Greendale, holiday trading hours or a seasonal offer.

Step 6: Earn reviews and reply to every one

Reviews affect both where you appear and whether people choose you. A steady flow of recent reviews is more convincing than an occasional burst.

  1. Copy the review link from your profile. It takes customers straight to the review form.
  2. Send it on WhatsApp with a short, friendly note as soon as each job is done.
  3. Turn it into a QR code for receipts, invoices and a card at the counter.
  4. Ask every customer, not only those you expect to be pleased. Asking only happy customers is against Google's policies.

Never buy reviews, offer discounts or gifts for them, or ask staff and relatives to write them. Google removes reviews it believes are fake and can take action against the profiles involved.

How to reply

Reply to every review within a day or two, and thank happy customers by name. With negative reviews, stay calm, because future customers are reading too: acknowledge the problem without arguing, offer a number to call or WhatsApp, and never share personal details. Google won't remove a review just because it's negative, but you can report one that breaks its policies, such as spam.

Step 7: Keep your name, address and phone the same everywhere

Google builds its picture of your business partly from information across the web, including directories. If your name, address and phone number (often called NAP) differ from site to site, they're harder to trust.

  • Write each detail one way and copy it everywhere. For customers abroad, use the international phone format: +263, then the number without its first 0.
  • Check your website, Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp Business profile, LinkedIn, Zimbabwean business directories and industry association listings.
  • Claim listings on other map services where you can, such as Bing Places.
  • Keep a spreadsheet of every listing, so changes reach all of them quickly.

Step 8: Give each area its own page on your website

If you serve several towns or suburbs, create a page for each, but only where you have something specific to say: what you offer there, how quickly you can arrive, the suburbs you cover, any call-out or delivery charges, photos of real jobs nearby and how to reach you. Don't copy one page and change only the town name. Google's spam policies warn against near-identical "doorway" pages like these.

Link each branch profile to its own page, and add LocalBusiness structured data so search engines can read your details clearly. If your current site makes this hard, our website development team can help.

Step 9: Track calls, direction requests and enquiries

Your profile's Performance section shows how many people found you, the searches they used, and how many called, asked for directions or clicked through to your website. Compare month to month, and remember these figures count taps, not sales.

  • Add tracking tags to your profile's website link, for example ?utm_source=google&utm_medium=organic&utm_campaign=gbp, so Google Analytics shows those visits separately.
  • Track clicks on your phone and WhatsApp buttons as events in Google Analytics.
  • Ask every new customer how they found you, and write it down.

Our Google Analytics and tracking service can set this up for you.

A simple routine to keep it working

TaskHow often
Reply to new reviewsWithin a day or two
Publish a postEvery week or two
Add new photosMonthly
Check your details, including any changes Google has madeMonthly, and before public holidays
Compare Performance figures with your enquiry recordsMonthly
Check directory listingsEvery three months

Nobody can promise a fixed spot on the map, because Google controls the results, but a complete, active and well-reviewed profile gives you a fair chance. If you'd rather hand it over, talk to our local SEO team, or contact us to book a free strategy session.
faqs: How long does it take to appear on Google Maps?

Once your profile is verified, it can start appearing for searches of your business name fairly quickly. Ranking for wider searches, such as "electrician in Harare", usually takes steady work over several months and depends on how many competitors you have and how active they are. Nobody can honestly promise you a date or a position.
Can I get on Google Maps if I work from home or don't have a shop?

Yes, as long as you meet customers in person, for example at their homes, sites or offices. Hide your address and set a service area instead. Businesses that operate only online aren't eligible for a Google Business Profile.
Can my staff or family leave reviews for the business?

No. Google's policies don't allow reviews from people with a conflict of interest, such as owners and staff, or reviews given in exchange for discounts or gifts. Reviews from relatives aren't honest feedback either. Ask real customers after real jobs, every time, and let your reviews build up honestly.

title: Marketing to Zimbabweans abroad: a practical guide for local businesses
seo_title: Marketing to the Zimbabwean Diaspora: A Practical Guide
description: How Zimbabwean businesses can sell to Zimbabweans abroad: what they buy, building trust, clear payment, WhatsApp sales, ad targeting and timing.
intro: Many Zimbabweans living in South Africa, the UK, the US, Australia and elsewhere regularly pay for things at home: groceries for parents, school fees, stands, building materials, solar systems and funeral cover. Given the choice, plenty would rather pay a reliable business directly than send cash and hope it's spent as planned. This guide shows how a Zimbabwean business can earn their trust and turn it into steady, repeat orders.
body:
Who you're really selling to

Your typical customer is a working adult abroad supporting parents, children in school or the wider family. Every sale involves two people: the buyer, who pays from abroad and wants proof the money did what it was meant to, and the recipient, who receives the goods and reports back. Both need a good experience. Some buyers have been away for years, so don't assume they know current prices or how things work locally.

What they buy for family back home

Each purchase comes with its own worry. Answer it in your marketing before the buyer has to ask.

What they buyWhat worries themWhat reassures them
Groceries and hampersWill it all arrive, fresh and complete?An itemised list, a delivery photo and a message from the recipient
School feesHas the school really been paid?Paying the school directly, and sending the school's own receipt
Stands and housesIs the land genuine, and is it the seller's to sell?Documents explained plainly, a video site tour and advice to use their own lawyer
Building materialsWill the full order reach the site?A delivery note matching the invoice, and photos of the materials on site
Funeral coverWhat's covered, and will it pay out quickly?Clear policy wording, who underwrites it and a simple claims process
Solar systemsWill it be installed properly, and who fixes it later?An itemised quote, installation photos, a written warranty and an after-sales contact

Trust is the main barrier, so build it on purpose

Buyers abroad can't walk into your shop, and many have heard stories of money sent home that went missing. Expect to be checked, and make checking easy.

  • Show you're real: your registered company name, a physical address in Zimbabwe, a phone that's answered, and a website and email on your own domain.
  • Show real faces: a short video of the owner and team, and a live video call so buyers can see the stock, warehouse or stand before they pay.
  • Prove every delivery with a photo or short video of the handover, taken with the recipient's permission.
  • Publish your policies on refunds, substitutions, delays and cancellations.
  • Protect your payment details: use only accounts in the business's name, publish them on your website, and say you'll never change them by message alone.
  • Let people start small. A hamper is an easier first yes than a stand deposit.

Many buyers will also check your Google reviews, and our local SEO service can help you build genuine ones.

Make payment and delivery impossible to misunderstand

Confusion about money is where trust breaks fastest. Before anyone pays, they should know:

  • the full price in US dollars, including delivery and fees, with nothing added later
  • which payment methods you accept from abroad, and how long each takes to clear
  • when delivery happens, and which areas you cover
  • what happens if an item is out of stock
  • what the recipient must do, such as be home or sign for the goods
  • what proof they'll get: an invoice, a receipt and delivery confirmation

Put all of this on one "How it works" page and send the link in your first WhatsApp reply, or let an e-commerce store with international payments and set delivery zones answer these questions for you.

WhatsApp is your shop counter

For many diaspora buyers, WhatsApp is where questions get asked and orders placed, so run it like a staffed counter.

  • Use the WhatsApp Business app, with your address, hours and website in your profile.
  • Build a catalogue with photos and prices, so buyers can browse without waiting.
  • Save quick replies for common questions, set an away message that says when you'll reply, and use labels to track orders: enquiry, quote sent, paid, delivered.
  • Use one official number on your website, ads, Google profile, receipts and vehicles.
  • Answer when buyers are free: a US buyer's evening falls in your night, and an Australian buyer's evening is your late morning or early afternoon.

Only send promotions to people who've opted in, and make opting out easy. Busier teams can move to the WhatsApp Business Platform, usually through a provider, to automate messages. Our email and WhatsApp marketing team can set up either.

Target by country on Meta and Google

Run a separate campaign for each country. Pay days, time zones and currencies differ, and separate campaigns let you set the budget and see the results for each market.

Meta: Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp

  • Set the location to the country, or to the cities where your customers live.
  • Use ads that open a WhatsApp chat.
  • Build audiences from website visitors, people who engaged with your page and customers who agreed to hear from you, and let Meta find similar people in each country.
  • Don't rely on interest settings to find Zimbabweans. They change, and your own audiences plus ads that clearly mention Zimbabwe are more dependable.

Google

  • Target the country your buyers live in, choosing people in or regularly in that location.
  • Use keywords that name Zimbabwe or a town, such as "groceries delivered to Harare" or "stands for sale in Harare".
  • Schedule ads for the buyer's hours, not Harare's.
  • Send each country's clicks to a landing page written for that country.

Tag links by country so you can see which market brings paying customers, not just clicks. Our paid ads team runs diaspora campaigns on both platforms.

Time it around pay days, school terms and holidays

Ask your customers when they're paid. As a starting point:

MarketTime compared with HararePay patterns to check
South AfricaSame timeMonthly pay is common, often towards the end of the month
United Kingdom1 or 2 hours behind, depending on the seasonMonthly pay is common
United States6 to 10 hours behind on the mainlandMany people are paid every two weeks
Australia6 to 9 hours ahead, depending on city and seasonFortnightly pay is common
  • School terms: most schools run three terms, starting around January, May and September. Promote fee payments a few weeks before each term, and check each year's official dates.
  • The festive season: start hamper campaigns in early November and publish a firm cut-off date for Christmas delivery.
  • Mother's Day: the UK marks it in March or early April, but South Africa, the US and Australia mark it in May, so plan each country separately.

Content and testimonials: real ones only

Useful content answers questions buyers are too polite to ask: a "how it works" video, delivery handovers filmed with permission, dated building progress updates, stand walk-arounds and price updates on WhatsApp Status.

Real testimonials are some of the most convincing content you can have. Never invent, borrow or "improve" them: fakes are dishonest, can break advertising and consumer rules, and one exposed fake can undo years of goodwill. Collect real ones with every order instead:

  1. A few days after delivery, ask the buyer how it went.
  2. If they're happy, ask for a sentence, a voice note or a short video.
  3. Get written permission to use their words, first name, country and photo, and keep a record.
  4. Ask the recipient too: a mother in Gweru confirming her hamper arrived means a lot to the next buyer.

Never change a testimonial's meaning, never use stock photos as "customers", and hide phone numbers in screenshots.

Start with one product, one country and one well-run WhatsApp number, then grow from there. If you'd like help planning it, contact us to book a free strategy session.
faqs: Which country should we target first?

Start where you already have customers or enquiries. If you have none yet, ask your local customers where their relatives abroad live. One well-run campaign in one country usually teaches you more than a small budget spread thinly across four.
Should we price in US dollars or in the buyer's currency?

US dollars are usually simplest, because many prices in Zimbabwe are already set in US dollars. If you also accept pounds, rand or other currencies, explain how the exchange rate is set and when it's fixed, so the buyer isn't surprised by the final amount.
How do we get testimonials if we're just starting out?

Ask your first customers directly after a successful delivery, and get their permission in writing before you use anything. Until you have some, show other proof instead: your team, your premises, delivery photos and clear policies. Never invent a testimonial or borrow one from another business.
